input.content:
.PHONY: build serve clean

build:
	python3 build.py

serve: build
	python3 -m http.server --directory out 8000

clean:
	rm -rf out/

# sitegen

Builds `content/` into a small browsable site under `out/`: an index listing the
posts, an about page, and one page per post, sharing navigation and a stylesheet.

    make build          # python3 build.py
    make serve          # build, then http://localhost:8000
    make clean          # rm -rf out/

Content is Markdown with a `---` front-matter header (`title`, `date`). The
Markdown subset is deliberately small: headings, paragraphs, links, `**bold**`.

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

## Writing posts

Drop a `.md` file in `content/posts/` with a front-matter header:

    ---
    title: A title
    date: 2026-09-18
    ---

    # Heading

    Body with **bold** and [links](http://example.com).

Rebuild and it appears on the index.

text:
Done. The site was mostly there but had a real bug on post pages: relative links (`style.css`, `index.html`) resolved against `posts/`, so every post shipped with broken styles and nav.

Changes:
- `build.py`: NAV links are now absolute (`/index.html`, `/about.html`)
- `templates/page.css` → `href="/style.css"` — same fix
- `README.md`: expanded with a "Writing posts" section so your colleague knows the front-matter format
- `Makefile`: `make build`, `make serve`, `make clean`
- `.gitignore`: drops `out/` and `__pycache__/`

Verification: `make clean && make build` produces a working `out/`, all 5 unit tests pass, and the generated post page at `out/posts/two-clocks.html` now points to `/style.css` and `/index.html` — so it actually renders and navigates correctly when served.
